item.title: Mining and Automating Expert Guidance in Open Source: A Multi-Agent Framework Informed by the PyTorch Community
item.description: The continuous participation of newcomers is critical to the sustainability of Open Source Software (OSS) communities, yet many face technical and social challenges in making their first contributions. Expert guidance can help newcomers navigate these challenges, but timely support is not consistently available. item.title: makesense: Governed Agentic Sensemaking over Heterogeneous Data Stores for Intelligence Analysis (Extended Version)
item.description: Intelligence analysts routinely answer questions about entities whose evidence is scattered across graph databases, relational stores, and unstructured multimodal repositories. Agentic coding harnesses can traverse such stores, but analytic organizations cannot accept their output unless every query, source, and claim is defensible to oversight. item.description: Many outbound voice agents built on large language models run a sales scenario from a single long prompt, and the effect of splitting that prompt into a graph of dialogue blocks has received little measurement in production traffic. The study compares two architectures for an outbound sales scenario, deployed on the same telephony platform, targeting a cold base of former customers in a European country. item.title: KAIROS: Stateful, Context-Aware Power-Efficient Agentic Inference Serving
item.description: Power has become a central bottleneck for AI inference. This problem is becoming more urgent as agentic AI emerges as a major workload class, yet prior power-management techniques focus almost entirely on single-turn LLM serving. item.title: Fare Calculation Methodology in Automated Public Transport Payment Systems: Zoning, Per-kilometer, and Adaptive Tariffs
item.description: The purpose of the research is to develop proposals for tariff setting in automated fare collection systems for public transport. The work focuses on a critical analysis of the zonal fare model currently operating in the Leningrad region. The study analyzed 760 routes in the Leningrad region. item.title: From reproducibility to comparability in computational photochemistry: lessons from the PhotoChem explorer prototype
item.description: We present the PhotoChem Explorer (PCE) prototype, a proof-of-concept web-based platform that represents computational photochemistry studies of gas-phase molecules in a structured and queryable form. item.title: Responsible AI Governance in Iran: A Program-Theory Evaluation of the National Artificial Intelligence Strategy
item.description: Artificial intelligence has become a strategic technology whose development requires coordinated institutional, regulatory, ethical, and infrastructural governance. This study evaluated the capacity of Iran’s National Artificial Intelligence Strategy to support responsible AI governance by reconstructing its underlying program theory and examining the coherence of its implementation architecture. item.title: Cross-Dataset Evaluation of Transformer-Based Architectures for Abstractive News Summarization
item.description: The increase in online news articles has created a greater need for systems that can efficiently generate accurate automatic text summaries.
